title: Broadcom's Custom AI Chip Business Is Bigger Than the Market Thinks
excerpt: With AI semiconductor revenue on track to hit $56 billion in fiscal 2026 and bookings outpacing shipments 3-to-1, Broadcom's XPU platform is cementing its position as the backbone of hyperscaler custom silicon.
body:
• Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue hit $10.8 billion in Q2 fiscal 2026, up 143% year-over-year, with full-year guidance raised to $56 billion — approximately 180% growth from fiscal 2025
  • Q2 bookings exceeded $30 billion against $10.8 billion shipped, giving Broadcom a roughly 3-to-1 book-to-bill ratio with visibility now extending into 2028
  • Six major customers are locked in: Google (1+ GW in 2026), Anthropic (5 GW starting 2027), OpenAI (1.3 GW in 2027, 10 GW by 2029), Meta (3 GW by end-2028), and two undisclosed clients with $6 billion in combined orders
  • Morningstar raised its fair value estimate to $650 per share, calling Broadcom's $100 billion fiscal 2027 guidance a "sandbag" and modeling close to $200 billion in AI chip revenue by fiscal 2028

Broadcom's custom AI chip business is growing faster than Wall Street can keep up with. The company's fiscal Q2 results showed AI semiconductor revenue of $10.8 billion — a $2.4 billion jump in a single quarter — while management guided for $16 billion in Q3 and raised the full-year fiscal 2026 target to $56 billion.

Yet shares fell 14% after hours following the June 3 earnings report. The reason: investors wanted more than the "more than $100 billion" fiscal 2027 guidance management reiterated. Analysts at Morningstar called the selloff "an overreaction to conservative guidance" and raised their fair value estimate to $650 per share.

The Custom Silicon Thesis

Broadcom doesn't compete directly with Nvidia on general-purpose GPU accelerators. Instead, it designs custom AI chips — called XPUs — built to the exact specifications of hyperscale customers. It holds approximately 70% of the custom AI accelerator market.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=66L4GMrU570

The business model is often described as a toll road: Google doesn't want to build its own semiconductor manufacturing operation. It wants bespoke silicon tuned to its specific inference workloads, and Broadcom designs and delivers it at scale. The same dynamic plays out with Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, and others.

"Customer demand for XPUs and AI networking devices is simply insatiable."

— Hock Tan, CEO, Broadcom

CEO Hock Tan laid out unprecedented specificity on deployment plans during the Q2 earnings call. Google will use over 1 gigawatt of Broadcom TPU compute in 2026, backed by a multi-generation long-term agreement signed in April. Anthropic will receive 5 gigawatts of next-generation TPU compute starting in 2027. OpenAI's chips have completed design and enter mass production by year-end, with 1.3 gigawatts deployed in 2027 as part of a "10 gigawatts by 2029" mega-deal.

Meta has committed to deploying 3 gigawatts of its MTIA XPU by the end of 2028, with the first 1-gigawatt order beginning delivery in the second half of 2027. Two additional undisclosed customers have placed orders worth $6 billion combined.

The Numbers That Matter

The book-to-bill ratio tells the real story. In Q2, Broadcom received over $30 billion in AI semiconductor orders against $10.8 billion shipped — nearly three times the shipment volume. Order visibility has extended from 2027 three months ago to 2028 now.

Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenue in the second half of fiscal 2026 to roughly double the first half. Morningstar models close to $120 billion in AI revenue in fiscal 2027 and nearly $200 billion by fiscal 2028, driven primarily by the Anthropic and OpenAI ramps.

Networking is also a significant growth driver, accounting for nearly 40% of Q2 AI revenue. Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 switch chip — the world's first 102.4 Tbps single-chip Ethernet switch — enables clusters of up to one million AI accelerators and has seen strong uptake across hyperscale deployments.

The Google Diversification Question

One concern weighing on investors: reports that Marvell has secured part of the design work for Google's next-generation TPU, suggesting Google is diversifying its supply chain. Tan addressed this directly.

"We are perfectly comfortable with the fact that, given the pace at which AI compute is being consumed, it is entirely foreseeable for a customer like Google to have diversified supply sources," he said. He pointed to the long-term agreement signed in April, which covers multiple generations of TPU and AI networking products with "very substantial committed amounts."

Investment Outlook

Morningstar rates Broadcom as a wide-moat business and one of its top semiconductor picks. The analyst note flags one structural risk: gross margins could compress into the 72-73% range as the custom chip mix rises, since XPUs are gross margin-dilutive though operating margin-accretive through customer co-investment.

Apollo and Blackstone are now helping finance purchases of Broadcom chips, which could amount to 20 gigawatts of capacity alone over the next two years. If the hyperscaler shift toward custom silicon is still in its early growth phase — and the booking data suggests it is — a single quarter's guidance variance looks less like a miss and more like noise.
